defects.justification: The private-address check resolves the host once with InetAddress.getAllByName and then http.send (line 224) resolves it again, so DNS rebinding bypasses it; the denylist also misses IPv6 unique-local fc00::/7, IPv4-mapped/NAT64 forms and CGNAT 100.64/10, leaving internal services reachable from a client-supplied URL.

Output height is derived from the source aspect ratio with no cap, and upscaling to 4096 is allowed; a tiny 1x100 source requested at width 4096 allocates a 4096x409600 ARGB BufferedImage (~6.7 GB), and up to 10 widths x 8 threads can run at once, so the MAX_PIXELS input check does not bound memory.

HttpRequest.timeout (line 221) only bounds the wait for response headers; with BodyHandlers.ofInputStream the body is then read by readLimited with no deadline, so a remote server that trickles bytes ties up one of the 8 worker threads indefinitely.

Every distinct uploaded image or URL creates a new cache directory of PNGs (up to 10 widths of 4096 px) and nothing ever evicts them; unauthenticated clients can fill the disk by posting varied inputs.

The missing-width check (line 164) and the render/move are not synchronised per id, so concurrent requests for the same source both render; Files.move with only ATOMIC_MOVE and no REPLACE_EXISTING may throw FileAlreadyExistsException on platforms that do not replace, turning a valid request into a 500.
Returned thumbnail URLs are built from the client-controlled Host header and hard-coded http://, so a forged Host yields links to an attacker domain (and links are wrong behind TLS or a proxy).
The HttpServer runs on a fixed pool of 8 threads with no read/idle timeout, and uploads of up to 20 MB are read synchronously; a handful of slow-upload clients exhausts the pool.
